text:
micah: kicking off a microburst replay run to investigate batching fairness across tenants. using 1k tenants, skewed traffic (90/9/1), replayer v2. no model changes, same GPU pool. noticed small QPS tenants are getting aggregated into huge batches and then starved for CPU time.
olivia: can you paste the replay config? especially max_delay / batch_cap settings.
micah: sure — current harness: 
```
replay: v2
tenants: 1000
traffic_shape: power_law(0.9)
max_delay_ms: 10
batch_size_cap: 64
kernel_hint: auto
kv_cache: enabled
replay_seed: 42
```
results in this run: overall p50 token-latency ≈ 70ms, p95 ≈ 420ms, but low-qps tenants p95 blows to ~1.2s.
raj: hm kernel_hint=auto could pick a large-fused kernel optimized for big batches, that hurts small-tenant tail. try forcing smaller-kernel or single-threaded GEMM for small batches to see if tail improves.
maya: also want to confirm KV cache behavior — small tenants won't share prefixes, so cache hit rate for them is near 0, which increases compute per request. that interacts badly with batching heuristics.
hun: agree. in prior runs we saw KV cache disabled made the p95 for small tenants worse but p50 stayed same. can you dump per-tenant kv_hit_rate and batch_size distribution?
micah: attaching quick dump (sample):
```
tenant_bucket: high-qps (10 tenants) -> avg_batch 48, kv_hit 0.8
tenant_bucket: mid-qps (90 tenants) -> avg_batch 16, kv_hit 0.25
tenant_bucket: low-qps (900 tenants) -> avg_batch 6, kv_hit 0.02
```
eng-bench-bot: replay run 1768009999 complete — summary: total RPS 4.2k, avg tokens/sec/gpu 72k, error rate 0.0%.
olivia: are you doing apples-to-apples? need to lock model version, quantization, kernel selection, and run on same seed/hardware. small changes break comparability.
micah: yes model pinned to open-ggml-v1 q4_0. kernel selection left auto to mirror prod. good point though — I'll run a controlled set with kernel_hint=[small_batch, large_batch, auto].
raj: suggestion: add per-tenant max-delay decay: if a tenant waits > X ms, reduce their batch cap to prefer smaller batches so they can go sooner. essentially per-tenant fast-path.
hun: or use weighted fair queueing based on recent latency — give low-qps tenants higher scheduling weight to avoid infinite wait. but that will cost throughput.
maya: tradeoff graph would help. can we run sweep across batch_cap {16,32,64} and max_delay {5,10,20} and record p50/p95/p99 per-tenant-bucket? also run with kv_cache off/on to isolate effect.
micah: running sweep now (kickoff). quick local profiling shows CPU steal during giant batches — kernel selection moves to multi-threaded path causing context churn. adding a flag to prefer single-threaded kernels for batch < 24 helped earlier.
eng-bench-bot: measurement note: use 30s steady state after 60s ramp to avoid startup artifacts.
olivia: also capture queue length histogram and the continuous-batching window distribution. we need to see how often the runtime waits the full max_delay vs flushes earlier due to batch_cap.
micah: FYI: small quick result from first sweep:
```
config: batch_cap=32, max_delay=10ms
overall p95: 380ms
low-qps p95: 780ms -> improved from 1.2s
throughput change: -2.1%
cpu utilization: +3%
```
maya: that's promising — small perf cost for much better fairness. can you also try per-tenant prioritization weight= min(1.0, 0.5 + 1/qps) to bias scheduler?
raj: also consider kernel selection policy hook: if batch_size < 24 use kernel_variant=A (low-latency), else B (throughput).
that keeps tail down without hurting throughput for big batches.
hun: need to be careful about quantization path differences — some kernels degrade perplexity slightly. add a quality check (eval prompts) in the sweep.
micah: added eval set. will run the full matrix and post results here. ETA ~40m.
olivia: ok great. one more meta: include a short reproducibility checklist in the thread for future runs: seed, git commit, model, quant, hw, plumbing (disable autoscaler), bench-bot label. makes apples-to-apples easier.
micah: noted. will post final CSVs and a small PR with scheduler flag toggles. action items: 1) micah run full sweep + upload CSVs; 2) raj prototype kernel hook; 3) hun add eval quality check; 4) olivia add reproducibility checklist to bench README.
maya: :thumbsup: thanks everyone. let's reconvene after results.
